title: Audio-Language Models — Qwen2.5-Omni, Audio Flamingo, GPT-4o Audio
service: LALMKit: decoder inputs with audio slots, a SQLite store of raw benchmark outputs, MMAU-style multiple-choice scoring, a budgeted live audio + text context, and nested multimodal message flattening

parts.lesson_anchor: The three-component template (encoder -> projector -> LLM taking interleaved text + audio tokens); Step 1 apply_chat_template; Step 2 projector; code/main.py interleave_with_text; quiz Q9 (frames and downsampling) and Q11 (expanding an AUDIO slot between start/end markers)
planted_bugs: audio_tokens floors num_frames / stack while stack_frames zero-pads the last run; the ValueError surfaces two calls later in merge (4 audio vectors for 3 AUDIO_PAD positions), whose check is correct
expand puts every clip in front of the text, as the lesson's interleave_with_text does, instead of widening each AUDIO slot where it stands
pad_batch builds the attention mask from token != PAD, but PAD = EOS, so a real EOS inside a row is masked and the positions derived from the mask go wrong too
pad_batch recomputes the mask's prefix sum for every position, O(L^2)
parts.timing_assert: pad_batch on a ten-minute clip (15,004 ids) plus a short row under 0.02 s; the per-token prefix sum takes about 0.5 s, the length-based version about 0.2 ms (an explicit-loop fix about 1.1 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: the merged ids and vectors must include every clip's zero-padded last token, which rules out cutting the audio to the slots in merge or dropping the partial run in stack_frames; a stack=3 check rules out (n + 1) // stack

parts.lesson_anchor: Step 3: write predictions to a model_output column for the official MMAU-Pro evaluator; Benchmark reality check; quiz Q16 (independent re-verification, control variables)
parts.exactness: raw model outputs round-trip byte for byte across close and reopen (leading spaces, CRLF, trailing space and newline), and a failed call (None) stays distinct from an empty answer ('')

parts.lesson_anchor: Where LALMs are not useful yet: real-time streaming reasoning; long-audio degradation; 50 encoder frames per second eats the context (quiz Q9)
parts.wire_format: after every event, a fresh list of the ids the decoder would see: turn ids as given, each clip as AUDIO_BOS + one AUDIO_PAD per audio token + AUDIO_EOS (Part 1's expand layout); the test compares them by event index

deviations: Part 1: the encoder frame count from samples is correct in the starter, because the encoder frame count belongs to 06/05's Part 1. The off-by-one sits between the processor's token count and the projector's zero-padded stacking, the mismatch the real merge step checks.
Part 1: the lesson's own interleave_with_text (all audio in front of the text) is added as the second planted bug, since the exam spec prefers bugs from the lesson's code.
Part 1: position ids are covered by the mask-derived positions and the timing assert (the per-token prefix sum), not by a separate position-id off-by-one, which kept the part at four bugs.
Part 3: per-category chance (the mean of 1 / len(choices)) is reported next to accuracy, from the lesson's 25%-on-4-options point; the lesson's MCQ filter decides which items are scored.
Part 4: the output is the decoder's id sequence, one fresh list per event, instead of a text wire format; 06/03 already uses NDJSON and 06/06 RTTM, and the id layout is the one Part 1 builds.
